title: Should schools teach more practical things?

items: It was **a complete waste of time**.
You **never know when it might come in handy**.
I **picked it up on the job**.
I **read up on** it. I **did my homework**.
It's **out of date**. You need to **adapt**.
**than you'd think** /ðən juːd ˈθɪŋk/ – «…, чем кажется» (= more/-er than people expect)
**It's been ages!** How have you been?
**I've been meaning to get in touch** for ages.
So, **what have you been up to?**

blocks.instr: Good lines from Friday. Which two could you say too — and why?
task: ❤️  Most of what I know, I **picked up on the job** — but I wouldn't say it was the hard way: I learned a lot from my colleagues.
❤️  **You never know when it might come in handy.** ((two of you built this one together))
❤️  I find teaching myself works better: I can **read up on** the subject as much as I want.
❤️  Learning English without dancing was **a steep learning curve** :-)
❤️  **Back in my day**, everyone was expected to get a solid education — and it really mattered.
❤️  At the end of the day, what we learned meant nothing. It was **out of touch with real life**.
❤️  Maybe it would be more useful to learn some **hands-on** skills, like how to cook, sew on a button or hammer in a nail.
❤️  Schools should probably also teach children how to **adapt** — no one actually knows what the future holds.

blocks.summary: Could be better → perfect: the full list
blocks.instr: One more of our sentences. Green = good, grey = could be better. Say the grey part with a phrase from the box (the word in red).

cards.ctx: чешский похож на русский — казалось, будет легко
cards.front: <g>For me it was Czech.</g> ~~I thought it's easy to learn a language which is similar.~~
cards.back: For me it was Czech. **It's really close to Russian, but it's a lot harder than you'd think.**
cards.why: harder than you'd think = what anyone expects vs reality. About your own past expectation: I thought it would be easy. ((«сложнее, чем кажется»))
cards.turn: Your turn: a language, a city or a job that was harder than you'd think. Why?

cards.instr: And this one? No red word this time.
cards.ctx: чему учишься на работе: говорить с менеджерами без технического бэкграунда
cards.front: <g>Communication with non-technical managers</g> — it's ~~harder than I was thinking~~.
cards.back: Communication with non-technical managers — it's **a lot harder than you'd think**.
cards.why: than I was thinking is a calque. Anyone would think so → than you'd think; only you → than I thought. ((калька с «чем я думала»))
cards.turn: Your turn: one thing at work or at home that's a lot harder than you'd think.

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?
cards.ctx: управлять людьми учишься у своих руководителей
cards.front: <g>I picked up</g> how to manage staff <g>on the job</g>, from my general managers. ~~You can't learn it at uni.~~
cards.back: I picked up how to manage staff on the job, from my general managers. **University only gets you so far.**
cards.why: You can't learn it at university is correct. The box phrase says more: university gives you the basics, the rest comes on the job. ((вуз даёт базу — дальше на работе)) · staff ##/stɑːf/## (AmE ##/stæf/##) — персонал · stuff ##/stʌf/## — вещи
cards.turn: Your turn: one thing you picked up on the job — not at university or school.

cards.instr: And this one? No red word this time.
cards.ctx: зачем работать на полный день, ещё учась в вузе
cards.front: ~~I understood that just studying at university isn't enough for me~~, <g>so I found a full-time job</g>.
cards.back: I **realised** that **university only gets you so far**, so I found a full-time job.
cards.why: understood → realised (it became clear to you); isn't enough for me → only gets you so far. ((осознала · даёт базу — и не больше))
cards.turn: Your turn: your degree or your school — where did it only get you so far?

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?
cards.ctx: когда пишешь код вместе с ИИ
cards.front: <g>AI helps me make suggestions</g>, but ~~finally I choose the best one with my own experience~~.
cards.back: AI helps me make suggestions, but **choosing the best one — that's where I really add value**.
cards.why: finally in mid-sentence sounds like «наконец-то»; «в итоге» is in the end. add value = what you bring that AI can't. ((«вот где от меня польза»))
cards.turn: Your turn: in your work or your life now, where do you really add value?

cards.instr: And this one? No red word this time.
cards.ctx: что остаётся за топ-менеджерами, когда ИИ есть на всех уровнях
cards.front: <g>Networking, department heads, motivation</g> — ~~in this kind of area, I believe AI is still helpless~~.
cards.back: Networking, department heads, motivation — **that's where people still add value**.
cards.why: helpless is usually about people. The box phrase talks about what people do well, not what AI can't do. ((helpless — «беспомощный», обычно о людях))
cards.turn: Your turn: two things where people still add value — and AI doesn't, yet.

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?
cards.ctx: почему серьёзные документы не доверяют ИИ
cards.front: <g>Top managers still work with paper documents</g> — they could go to jail. ~~That's why we don't use AI for serious work.~~
cards.back: Top managers still work with paper documents — they could go to jail. **That's why we don't hand anything serious over to AI.**
cards.why: hand sth over to AI = give AI the whole job, not just use it. ((«передать ИИ целиком»))
cards.turn: Your turn: one thing you'd never hand over to AI. Why not?

cards.instr: And this one? No red word this time.
cards.ctx: что ИИ теперь делает за тебя на работе
cards.front: Things that took me five hours <g>a couple of years ago</g>, ~~AI could do for five minutes~~.
cards.back: Things that took me five hours a couple of years ago, **I now hand over to AI — it does them in five minutes**.
cards.why: in five minutes = how long it takes to finish; for five minutes = how long it goes on. ((«за пять минут» — in five minutes))
cards.turn: Your turn: one task you've handed over to AI — or would love to.

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?
cards.ctx: что пригодилось из того, чему учились сами
cards.front: <g>This is touch typing.</g> ~~And it's very useful for typing.~~
cards.back: This is touch typing. **It comes in really handy.**
cards.why: very useful for typing repeats typing; it comes in handy = it turns out to be useful. Touch typing, not blind typing. ((«пригождается» · слепая печать — touch typing))
cards.turn: Your turn: a skill that came in really handy. When?

cards.instr: Could be better English: how would you say the grey part?
cards.front: <g>Children just go home, ask AI and write it down.</g> ~~It's useless at all.~~
cards.back: Children just go home, ask AI and write it down. **So what's the point of homework?**
cards.why: at all goes with not and questions (not useful at all). What's the point of…? = «какой смысл в…?» ((«какой смысл в…?»))
cards.turn: Your turn: something where you thought: what's the point of this?

blocks.instr: If you're done: in pairs. Use the box.
items: **1**  Go back through the ten sentences: say each upgrade without looking.
**2**  Which of the ten sentences is closest to your own story — and which is furthest from it? Why?
**3**  Something you learned recently that has already **come in handy** — and something where you thought: **what's the point of** this?

blocks.instr: In rooms: read the situation. Quick vote: which two would you cut, and which two would you add? No reasons yet.

p: An international school is changing its curriculum. The head ((AmE: principal)) wants to cut coding and essay writing: “AI can do all that now.” Two new subjects could be added.

blocks.instr: What might they say? Use the box. Then tap the card.

cards.instr: At the school meeting: what might they say? Use the box. Then tap the card.
cards.back: **What's the point of** learning to code? A lot of tech companies have **stopped hiring juniors**. They're **handing all that work over to AI**. Whatever we learn now will be **out of date** by the time we graduate from university.

cards.ctx: **Omar, 52,** a parent. Runs a group of small hotels and does the hiring. Wants to add “how to learn”.
cards.back: I don't need people who know a particular booking system: it'll be **out of date** in two years. They need to **adapt**. I need people who can **read up on** something new and **teach themselves**.

cards.ctx: **Chloe, 24,** a former student. Her first job was in a call centre. Wants to add “dealing with difficult people”.
cards.back: Nobody prepared us for angry customers. I **had to learn the hard way**. And it would have been so easy to teach: two or three role-plays in class.

blocks.instr: In pairs, on the page: the dice tells you how many reasons to give, for and against. Use the box. Then agree on two to cut and two to add.
